observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a tennis racket whose frame and strings are coated in bright red powder, with a yellow-green tennis ball resting against the string bed, which is pressed into a deep concave bowl shape. A cloud of red powder billows around the strings and the ball against a blurred dark/green background.
visible_changes: The tennis ball moves steadily upward (and slightly leftward) relative to the racket, traveling from the middle of the string bed toward the top edge of the frame, where it becomes partly cropped out in the last frames.
The concave depression of the strings gradually relaxes and flattens as the ball rises, so the bowl-shaped deformation seen early is largely gone by the end.

The red powder cloud continuously expands and disperses: the dense powder ring clinging to the rim spreads outward and downward into a wider, more diffuse billowing haze that increasingly fills the area where the strings were.
The ball's seam orientation shifts slightly between frames, suggesting a small rotation, though this is subtle.
The racket body and its lower-left frame remain in place throughout; the background stays roughly static.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ball was struck before this segment or how the powder was applied is not shown.
The ball's eventual landing or the final dissipation of the powder cloud is not captured.
Any motion of the racket itself (e.g., a swing) prior to the first frame is unseen.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the slight leftward shift of the racket and ball across frames is camera movement or actual object translation; background evidence is too blurred to decide.
The exact cause of the powder dispersal (rebound of the strings vs. airflow) cannot be determined from the visible frames alone.
